objects.description: A named bundle of permitted actions, such as the one an owner holds or the one a read-only visitor holds. What it permits is the role_actions beside it; this row is only the name and why it exists.

fields.name: code
fields.description: Stable key for the bundle, such as owner or viewer. Fixed at creation — every grant names it.

fields.name: name
fields.description: What the bundle is called in a listing.

fields.name: description
fields.description: What holding this bundle lets someone do, in the domain's own words. A bundle nobody can explain is the one that grows.

fields.name: seeded
fields.description: Whether a seeding pass owns this bundle's actions and will rewrite them. A hand-made bundle is left alone.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the bundle was declared.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.description: When it last changed.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description: Whether it has been retired. A retired bundle permits nothing, and the grants naming it are kept so the trail survives.

objects.description: One action a bundle permits. Actions are listed one by one and never matched by pattern: a pattern is a permission that widens itself the next time somebody declares an operation.

fields.name: role_code
fields.description: The bundle this permission belongs to.

fields.name: action
fields.description: The declared action it permits, such as the one an operation names. Compared exactly, never interpreted.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: When the permission was added to the bundle.

indexes.name: role_action
indexes.description: The permission check: does this bundle permit this action.

objects.description: One subject holding one bundle in one scope. Grants only ever add: nothing here takes a permission away, because a rule that subtracts needs a precedence order, and a precedence order is where an access-control system stops being possible to reason about.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: Whoever authenticated, exactly as the caller supplied it. This module never interprets it and never resolves it to a person.

fields.name: scope
fields.description: Where the bundle applies, as an opaque key the caller chooses. Compared exactly, with one reserved value: a scope of * applies everywhere. A scope of the form record:<module>/<object>/<id> names one record and answers for that record alone.

fields.name: partition
fields.description: Which partition of the deployment the grant holds in, as an opaque key the caller chooses. Empty means every partition, which is what every grant made before partitions existed means. A grant naming one partition never answers a question asked in another, nor one asked in none.

fields.name: role_code
fields.description: The bundle held.

fields.name: granted_by
fields.description: The subject that made this grant, for the trail. Empty when a bootstrap made it, which is itself worth being able to see.

fields.name: granted_at
fields.description: When it was made.

fields.name: ends_at
fields.description: When the grant stops answering, as RFC 3339 text stored in UTC at a fixed width. Empty means it never ends. Past this instant no check honours the grant and no listing shows it, exactly as if it had been withdrawn.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description: Whether it has been withdrawn. Withdrawn grants are kept rather than removed, so a revocation leaves a trail of what was held and when it stopped.

indexes.name: subject_scope
indexes.description: The permission check's first half: every live bundle this subject holds here.

objects.description: Whether one role kind holds one permission in one partition, as one layer set it. Two layers exist: the published definition's and the owner's override; an override row, when present, is the answer. A permission is an opaque code naming a list of actions elsewhere; this module never learns what it allows.

fields.name: partition
fields.description: The partition the setting holds in, as an opaque key the caller chooses.

fields.name: permission
fields.description: The permission's code, compared exactly and never interpreted.

fields.name: role_kind
fields.description: The kind of role the setting is for, as an opaque key the caller chooses.

fields.name: layer
fields.description: Which layer set it: the published definition or the owner's override.

fields.name: held
fields.description: Whether that layer ticks the permission for that role kind.

fields.name: set_by
fields.description: The subject that set it, from the caller. Empty when a publish or bootstrap set it.

fields.name: set_at
fields.description: When it was last set.
